_doc: One entry per production widget found in the 0.7.5 captures. `named` is a key of the capture's layout.json `named` map (its rect is the widget); `rect` [x, y, w, h] is a hand-recorded crop for a widget with no named rect, and its derivation is written in `note`. `label` is the production text set on a scratch copy before rendering (in the text node `label_node`, default `Label`) so the hug width is comparable. `labels` {"<path>": "<text>"} sets several texts the same way, for a composite: a path is node names joined by `/` below the variant (`Review button/Label`, so the text of a nested instance is reachable), an unknown or ambiguous name fails the compare, and `label` and `texts` keep working beside it. `icon` is the production icon swapped in on a placed instance (the compare repaints the glyph in the variant's own colour: a swap drops it, engine bug #1427). `mask_glyph` ignores the centre 24 px of the colour figures. `render_rect` [x, y, w, h] compares only that part of the render, and `render_node` names the node it is cut from (node names joined by `/` below the variant, "" for the variant itself): the rect must equal that node's bounds in the saved file, or, for a window that is only a part of it, the bounds trimmed by `render_trim` [left, top, right, bottom] (a `null` edge is free: a window is pinned at its top-left corner and at every edge it shares with the node; crop_geometry), so a window that drifts from the component fails the run; `align` "fg" crops both images to their foreground first; `bg` [r, g, b] is the colour the render is composited over (default the page, 10 10 10); `colour_only` marks a glyph a custom painter draws: the box is exempt, the colours are compared. `kit` says whether the widget is painted by widgets/kit (true) or a legacy painter. `follows` maps each set to the Rust (`path-under-crates/designos-app/src::fn`) its look follows; the compare resolves each to file:line. A painter the app has removed, which the 0.7.5 captures still show, is pinned instead: `v0.7.5 <path>:<line> <fn> (removed by #<pr>)` (valid only while the function is gone from the tree). Every entry is checked for three things: the foreground box (glyph or label) of render and crop agree within 1 px, the surface colour (the colour most pixels have) agrees within 6 per channel, and the strongest pixel agrees within 8 (24 for `colour_only`). `fg_pending` "#1427" exempts the box AND both colours of an entry whose swapped icon is 20 px, only while #1427 is open: the swap resets the glyph to the icon main's 16 px, so the box is not measurable until the engine fix merges, and a thin 16 px glyph never reaches full coverage. The compare prints those rows. `finding` records why an entry differs from production and is printed with it; `finding_pin` pins the measured score fields it describes (`{"fg_render_px": [230, 16], "fg_production_px": [234, 16]}`): the run accepts a failing entry while every pinned field still equals the measurement and the pin holds every field of each check the entry fails, and exits 1 when a finding pins nothing or a pinned number moves (crop_report). `gradient` true marks a strip with no surface and no mark (a gradient): the box, surface and strongest-pixel checks do not apply, and the entry is compared pixel by pixel over the two crops' common size (mean difference at most 2.0, 99th percentile at most 8, sizes within 1 px; crop_gradient). `captures` is an entry's own capture folder (repo-relative, resolved like the top-level one; capture_dirs) for a picture that is not in the run's folder, such as the empty Home. `fg_inset` is the px cut off each edge before the foreground is searched (default 4); 0 for a label that touches the crop edge.
